description: Queues one solve per point and returns the sweep's number at once. A point is a list of edits (`{ "cmd": "set_param", "args": { "name": "w", "value": 4e-7 } }`: any command that changes the project except those that replace it or start work), applied to a copy of the project: what varies, a geometry parameter, the wavelength in the study, a material, a mesh setting, is the case's to decide. Give `points` (each `{ label, edits }`) or `series` (`{ cmd, args, field, values }`: the command repeated with `field` set to each value). `physics` is the code or list solved at every point (default: what a solve would solve). The points are queued at priority 3 (sweeps and batches) so a person's request and a single request of an agent go before them, and run on the same mesh and solve caches as any request. Every point's edits are applied and checked first: a bad point fails the request with its number and nothing runs. The project, the mesh and the results of the engine are not touched; each point is recorded in the run table when the project is bound to a workflow. Read the table with `sweep_table`.

A handle is a small value, not the field: it names the physics, the solution and the field, and is read from the stored result each time it is used. A name is a per-cell field of the solution (`Ex`, `uz`, ...: complex when the solve is) or else a flat field of `result_info` (`T`, `|E|`: real). A vector name (`E` when `Ex` and `Ez` exist) answers one handle per component.

An operand is a handle, a field name of `physics`/`solution`, a number, or another operation `{op, args}`. The operation is checked against the results and returned as one handle.

title: Arithmetic on handles

description: The integral of an expression of fields over a region (a region name, comma list or `name*`; default the whole mesh), with the degree-4 rule of the finite elements (exact for the product of two P2 fields). A real expression answers a number, a complex one [re, im]. `measure` is the area or volume of the region. `revolution: true` weights by 2 pi r for a body of revolution (a 2D r-z mesh). Answers `stale` and `age_s` of what it read. FORMULAS (every `expr` of the reductions takes one): a text such as `abs(Ex)^2 * eps_r` or `where(x > 0, T, 0)`, parsed once and evaluated at each point in Rust. Numbers (`2j` is imaginary), `pi`, `e`, `+ - * / ^`, comparisons, `and or not`; functions `abs abs2 re im conj sqrt exp sin cos arg log log10 tan sinh cosh tanh atan step min max atan2` and `where(cond, a, b)` (only the branch that applies is evaluated, so `where(x != 0, 1/x, 0)` is safe). Names: the coordinates `x y z`; the fields of the result (`Ex`, `T`; in backticks when the name is not an identifier, `` `|E|` ``; `` `ems:Ex` `` or `` `ems:1:Ex` `` in backticks for another physics or solution); material values by their descriptor name (`eps_r`, `rho`; `eps` means `eps_r`; `material("rho")` to be explicit); `region("Si")` is 1 inside the region and 0 outside. A name like `E` stands for the vector (Ex, Ey, Ez) when the solution has those components: `dot(a, b)`, `inner(a, b)` (conjugates a), `cross`, `norm(v)`, `norm2(v)`, `E.x`. Orders, comparisons, `log` and `tan` read real values: wrap a complex one in `abs`, `re` or `im`. A material value is the one the solver saw in each cell. A tensor property (`eps_r`, `k`, `alpha`) has its entries as `eps_r_xx`, `eps_r_yy`, `eps_r_zz`, `eps_r_xy`, `eps_r_xz`, `eps_r_yz` in wafer axes with the crystal orientation applied (an isotropic material is the scalar times the identity); the plain `eps_r` is refused on a mesh where some material is a tensor. BOUNDARY INTEGRALS: with `boundary` (an outer boundary such as "window.top", or an interface "oxide|silicon" between two regions) the sum is over the facets of the boundary instead of the cells: a line integral on a 2D mesh, a surface integral on a 3D one, with `revolution` weighting by 2 pi r. The formula may use `nx`, `ny`, `nz`, the unit normal in wafer axes, so the flux of a vector F is `dot(F, [nx, ny, nz])`. At an interface the fields and materials differ on the two sides, so give `side`, the region to read them in; the normal points out of it. On an outer boundary no `side` is needed. `wavelength` (m) reads the material values at that wavelength, not the study's; the fields stay those of the solve.

boundary.description: integrate over the facets of this boundary (an outer boundary name, or an interface "a|b" between two regions) instead of over cells: a line integral on a 2D mesh, a surface integral on 3D. The formula may use nx, ny, nz, the unit normal. Not with region

Replaces the present project. Needs a build with HDF5 support. With `wait` false it starts a job (reading and meshing happen on it; the project is replaced when job_wait or poll_jobs applies it).
